behaviors.question: How does audioService trigger file upload / media URLs and what base-URL/header transformation is applied by the imported index chunk?

claim_review.finding: It creates recording-<Date.now()>.wav and appends image, subfolder=audio and type=temp to FormData.
It calls api.fetchApi('/upload/image', {method: 'POST', body}) without explicit headers.
It accepts status 200, parses JSON and reads the name field.
Non-200 status adds an alert and throws; no local retry is present.

behaviors.utility: Concrete upload trigger, request body, success condition, error path and returned temp reference. The initial record correctly leaves fetchApi base/header handling unverified; that part is supplied by the second behavior.

behaviors.question: Where does api.user, sent as the Comfy-User header, originate?

claim_review.finding: initialize() reads api.getUserConfig() and localStorage Comfy.userId.
login writes userId/userName; logout deletes both keys.
watchEffect assigns api.user only when server config exposes users and a userId exists.
fetchApi injects Comfy-User and fetches api_base + /api + path. It supplies cache=no-cache by default, but a caller-provided cache value in the spread object can override it.
The value is client-selected and persisted locally; it is not proved server-authorized.
/prompt and /upload/image are supported by the delivered ranges; /extensions is not present in the cited ranges and cannot be verified from the selected delivery alone.
The constructor default is an empty user; without users the watch effect does not assign a value.
The record explicitly leaves server validation unverified.

behaviors.utility: Explains client-controlled identity propagation into every fetchApi request and correctly avoids claiming server authorization. One illustrative endpoint is overbroad relative to the delivered ranges.

summary.assessment: Both records contain concrete, source-backed behavioral information beyond endpoint discovery. The pair jointly covers upload construction and the API wrapper's user-header behavior without asserting server trust.
